sentences.text: This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 and 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 23.03.2022 at about 7.55 a.m. she was walking on extreme left side on K.H.Road, Shanthinagar Junction, Bengaluru, at that time, a autorickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-04-D-6803 came in rash and negligent manner without observing traffic rules and regulations and dashed against her, due to the impact, she fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the SCCH-5 body.

Immediately after the accident, she was taken to P.D.Hindhuja Sindhi Hospital, after firstaid she was shifted to St.John's Medical College Hospital, wherein she took treatment as inpatient and spent Rs.6,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, food and nourishment.
3. At the time of the accident, she was aged about 18 years, hale and healthy, studying Degree course at St. Joseph College.
Due to the accidental injuries, she is not able to do day-to-day activities and undergoing deep mental shock, pain and suffering and injuries caused are permanent in nature.
Out of this accident crime No.19/2022 is registered against the driver of said offending autorickshaw before the Wilson Garden Traffic Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279 & 338 of IPC.
Respondent is the R.C.Owner of the autorickshaw SCCH-5 bearing Reg. No.KA-04-D-6803 is liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.20,00,000/-
with interest.

4. On service of notice, respondent being the R.C.Owner of the autorickshaw bearing Reg.
No.KA-04- D-6803 has remained absent, hence placed exparte.
5. In order to prove her case, Petitioner herself deposed her evidence as PW-1 and marked 12 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.12 and closed her evidence.
On the other hand, respondent placed exparte, hence there is no evidence on respondent side.

6. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record.
7.

On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, the points that would arise for my consideration:
SCCH-5 ::POINTS::
1. Whether Petitioner proves that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 23.03.2022 at about 7.55 a.m. when she was walking at K.H.Road, Shanthinagar Junction, Bengaluru at that time, autorickshaw bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-D-6803 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the petitioner and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?

2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so how much and from whom?

8. Then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
Point No.1 : In the Affirmative Point No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Point No.3 : As per final order for the following:
SCCH-5 ::REASONS::
9. Point No.1:- In order to prove her case, petitioner has deposed her evidence as PW-1, in her chief-examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in her petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of seizure mahazar is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of Sec.133 notice is marked as Ex.P.7, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.10.

10 . On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and records those have marked i.e., FIR, complaint, charge sheet, seizure mahazar, sketch, spot mahazar, Sec.133 notice, SCCH-5 IMV Report corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 23.03.2022 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
11.
Per contra, inspite of service of notice, respondent being the owner of the autorickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-04-D-6803 has remained absent, hence placed exparte.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 23.03.2022 at about 7.55 a.m. when he was walking on extreme left side on K.H.Road, Shanthinagar Junction, Bengaluru.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
12. On the other hand, there is no defence evidence and the police papers speaks that, very accident SCCH-5 is occurred due to negligency of the driver of the accident bearing Reg. No.KA-04-D-6803.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the above point No.1 in her favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Point No.1 in the affirmative.
13. Point No.2:-

As per the case of the petitioner, she was aged about 18 years, for proof of her age,
she has not produced age proof documents, but on perusal of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.9,
age of the petitioner is mentioned as 19 years, accordingly relying on Ex.P.9 her age is considered about 19 years as on the date of accident.
Further it is the case of the petitioner that, she was studying Degree Course at St. Joseph College.
In SCCH-5 this regard, she has not exhibited any documents with regard to her studies is concerned.

sentences.text: As per the evidence of the petitioner, she had sustained traumatic brain injury (right FTP acute SDH), right FTP clavrial defect, for which she underwent surgery of right FTP decompressive craniectomy withy acutre SDH evacuation, right FTP titanium mould cranioplasty.

She has exhibited medical bills amounting to Rs.2,96,896/- and Rs.1,04,289/-, totally a sum of Rs.4,01,185/- are marked as Ex.P.11 and discharge summary marked as Ex.P.12 issued by St. John's Medical College Hospital wherein she took treatment as inpatient since 23.03.2022 to 08.04.2022 and from 26.12.2022 to 30.12.2022.
15.

Petitioner has not examined the Doctor who has treated her nor produced the disability certificate SCCH-5 towards the injuries sustained by her in the alleged accident, but on perusal of the facts, wound certificate, medical bills, discharge summary and evidence of PW-1 corroborated to believe the injuries sustained by the petitioner out of the accident.

Accordingly petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.xxxxx/- along with medical bills of Rs.4,01,185/-, Rs.15,000/-
towards pain and suffering and Rs.15,000/- towards food, conveyance and nourishment charges.
16. Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.4,81,185/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

17. In the case on hand, respondent being the R.C.Owner of the autorickshaw bearing Reg.
No.KA-04- D-6803 is directed to deposit the award amount with SCCH-5 interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Point No.2 partly in the affirmative.
18. Point No.3:

For the reasons assigned to points No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.4,81,185/-
(Rupees Four Lakhs Eighty One Thousand One Hundred Eighty Five only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to her account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall SCCH-5 be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in her name.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, typed by her, thereof is corrected and then pronounced by me in the Open Court on this the 10th day of February,
2025)

(MANJUNATHA K.P.) VIII ADDL. JUDGE, COURT OF SMALL CAUSES &
